problem: The fail-closed public English build correctly prevented untranslated /en/* content, but the full-site static translation path could overload the provider by running multiple large batches concurrently with short fixed retries.
root_cause: The static translator defaulted to four concurrent batches, only four short linear retry delays, and ignored provider Retry-After guidance. A full production build therefore created avoidable burst load and made a valid configured provider less reliable.
failed_approaches: Allowing four concurrent full-site translation workers by default.
Retrying provider failures after short fixed delays without honoring Retry-After.
Treating provider availability and provider-friendly request pacing as the same thing.
prevention: Production static translation defaults to one provider worker; concurrency can only be widened deliberately and remains capped.
Rate-limit, overload, timeout and server failures use bounded exponential backoff.
Provider Retry-After guidance is honored when present.
Translation batches are paced between successes instead of sent as a burst.
Production remains fail-closed: resilience may retry, but it may never publish untranslated English as success.
Every i18n resilience change reruns the exact production pricing/language browser proof.

evidence.production_env_verified: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exists with build scope; value intentionally not recorded.
evidence.provider_guidance: Anthropic documents 429 rate limits, 529 overload and exponential retry for server errors.
